newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Sinaloa, Sonora states plant soybeans-ASA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Sinaloa, Sonora states plant soybeans-ASA.

text.p: Mexico's northwestern states of Sinaloa and Sonora are planting and test planting soybeans this year after several years of avoiding the oilseed because of white fly, a source said Wednesday.
Local offices of the United Soybean Board and the American Soybean Association (USB/ASA) said in an update that two factors had triggered interest in sowing soybeans.
One factor is that one or more of the seed companies supplying the region are suggesting that one variety is somewhat but not totally resistant to white fly.

"Some farmers are willing to test the variety by planting some acreage in soybeans this year right in the middle of the white fly country," the USB/ASA said. No indication was given of how much land is being planted.
Also, Agroasemex, the Mexican insurance giant that covers agribusiness, is offering a 500 pesos per hectare policy that covers white fly for soybeans, USB/ASA said.

"The confirmation comes from an insurance broker that has some agricultural policies in place around the country. The policy...covers weather-related disasters and biological losses including white fly in soybeans," it added.
